## 1. STRICT RULES & ARCHITECTURE

**1.1 CSS-First Architecture & Zero Inline CSS**
- All styling lives in `style.css`; the `style="..."` attribute is forbidden in authored HTML. Styling targets class (BEM) selectors only; IDs are reserved for JS hooks and anchors.
- HTML stays semantic and style-agnostic: re-theming the site must be possible by editing CSS only, never the markup.
- **Runtime exception:** JS may update CSS custom properties (e.g., `element.style.setProperty('--pos', …)` for the slider and theme class on `<html>`) — that is runtime state, not inline CSS; no static `style=` attribute may ever appear in `index.html`.

**1.2 CSS Variables & Theme Tokens**
Define exactly the token sets from 0.2/0.3. Every light background token pairs with a dark text token and vice versa, enforced in both themes. Substituted-white rule (`#FEFEFE` over `#FFFFFF`) applies to every surface.

**1.3 Mandatory Dark Mode Support**
Dark tokens per 0.3 under `.dark` (plus the media-query fallback for first paint). Header toggle button: Material Symbol `dark_mode`/`light_mode` swap, correct `aria-pressed` and `aria-label` ("Switch to dark theme" / "Switch to light theme"), persisted in `localStorage` key `"theme"`, first-visit fallback to `prefers-color-scheme`, polite live-region announcement on switch. Include `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">` and update `<meta name="theme-color">` on toggle. Theme must flip with zero HTML restructuring and zero flash of the wrong theme.

**1.4 Flexbox Layout & Mobile-First Alignment**
- Build every layout with flexbox; every flex container defaults to `align-items: center`. Any deviation (e.g., `stretch` for equal-height card rows) requires a one-line CSS comment justifying it.
- Mobile-first: rows collapse to columns below 768px; fluid type/spacing via `clamp()`; content column max-width ~1140px; horizontal scrolling is forbidden (verify at 320px). Anchored sections get `scroll-margin-top` for the sticky header; enable `scroll-behavior: smooth` guarded by `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**1.5 Styling Approach (Framework Decision)**
Dependency-free custom CSS in `style.css` (chosen so the deliverable runs with no build step), organized in comment-delimited layers: tokens → base/reset → layout → components → utilities → animations → responsive. Raw hex values are permitted only inside the `:root`/dark token blocks; all component rules reference `var(--…)`.

**1.6 Typography & Icons — Google Only**
Google Fonts per 0.4 (with `<link rel="preconnect">` + one stylesheet link). Icons are exclusively **Google Material Symbols (Rounded)** via the official stylesheet; decorative icon spans get `aria-hidden="true"`, meaningful ones get text alternatives. Raw inline SVGs, local icon files, and emoji-as-icons are forbidden.

## 2. COMPONENT DESIGN SPECIFICATIONS

**2.1 Buttons**
Base `.btn`: flex; `align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem`; minimum 44×44px touch target; `var(--radius-md)`; font-weight 600. Variants: `.btn--primary` (background `var(--gradient-cta)`, color `#FEFEFE`), `.btn--outline` (2px border + text in `var(--primary-strong)`, transparent background), `.btn--ghost`, `.btn--icon` (44px square, for toggle/menu/close/social), `.btn--danger` (red fill, visually distinct in both themes — define it even though this page has no destructive action). States, all via CSS classes/pseudo-classes: hover (`brightness(1.08)` + `var(--shadow-sm)`, pointer cursor); focus-visible (2px `var(--focus-ring)` outline, offset 2px); active (`transform: scale(0.97)`); `.is-loading` (blocks re-clicks, swaps label to a spinning `progress_activity` icon without changing button dimensions); `[disabled]` (opacity 0.5, grayscale, `cursor: not-allowed`); `.is-success` / `.is-error` (transient ~1.5s feedback using `--text-success`/`--text-error`, always icon + text, never color alone).

**2.2 Cards**
Base `.card`: flex column, gap, padding `var(--spacing-gap)`, background `var(--bg-secondary)`, 1px `var(--border-default)`, `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--shadow-sm)`. Hover: `translateY(-2px)` + `var(--shadow-md)`; `:focus-within`: border shifts to `var(--primary-strong)` with a soft ring (for cards containing links/buttons); `.card--skeleton`: shimmer styling that reserves final dimensions (no layout jump); `.card--featured`: gradient-border pricing tier; `.card--empty`: centered fallback layout — large Material Symbol (`add_photo_alternate`) + one line of guidance text (used by the dropzone's initial state).

**2.3 Forms & Inputs**
`.input-group`: flex column wrapping `<label>`, the field, and a dedicated error container (`aria-live="polite"`). Input base: min-height 48px, `var(--radius-md)`, background `var(--bg-primary)`, 1px `var(--border-default)`. States: empty; focus (2px `var(--focus-ring)` ring + subtle glow); filled; valid (`--border-success` + `check_circle` icon); invalid (`--border-error`, `error` icon, error message in `var(--text-error)` — message text accompanies the color, never color alone); disabled; read-only. Email validation on blur and submit: empty → "Please enter your email address."; malformed → "That doesn't look like a valid email."; on success the submit button enters `.is-loading` (≥1s), then `.is-success` with a live-region confirmation message.

**2.4 Modal / Demo Lightbox**
Triggered by the hero's "See It in Action". Structure: `.modal` (fixed, inset 0, flex, `align-items: center; justify-content: center`, `var(--z-modal)`), backdrop (rgba(0,0,0,0.6) + `backdrop-filter: blur(4px)`), panel (background `var(--bg-primary)`, `var(--radius-lg)`, `var(--shadow-md)`, `width: min(92vw, 720px)`). States: opening (fade + scale 0.96→1 over `var(--transition-normal)`), open, loading (`.card--skeleton` shimmer while the "demo renders", `aria-busy`), success (before/after image pair with a single `.ai-transform-animation` sweep + caption), error (empty-state-style fallback: "Couldn't load the demo — check your connection."), closing (reverse animation, then hidden). UX: close button with `close` icon and `aria-label="Close dialog"`; `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby`; Esc and backdrop click close; keyboard focus trapped inside while open; focus returns to the trigger; body scroll locked.

## 3. CORE UX & MICRO-INTERACTION RULES

- **Responsive by default:** fluid `clamp()` sizing, flex wrapping, column stacking under 768px, zero horizontal overflow at any width.
- **Fluid transitions:** every hover/focus/active/state change animates with `var(--transition-fast)` or `var(--transition-normal)`. Optional scroll-reveal: `.reveal` elements fade/translate into view via IntersectionObserver adding `.is-visible` — disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`, which collapses all animations/transitions to near-zero duration.
- **Accessibility (a11y):** semantic landmarks (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `section[aria-labelledby]`, `footer`), skip link, logical heading order (one `h1`), visible `:focus-visible` everywhere, full keyboard operability (menu, dropzone as a button, native range slider, chips as toggles, modal focus trap), `aria-live` regions for dropzone status and form feedback, contrast ≥ 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large text in both themes, and state never communicated by color alone.
- **Mandatory visual feedback:** every interactive element responds visibly — buttons tint and lift, chips show selection (border, fill, `aria-pressed`), the compare handle scales while dragging, the dropzone glows during dragover, forms show loading→success. Never rely on hover alone (touch devices): pair every hover effect with `:focus-visible`/active feedback.
- **Drag-and-drop micro-interactions:** the dropzone reacts to `dragenter`/`dragover` (dashed `var(--primary)` border, glow, icon swap `add_photo_alternate` → `bolt`), `dragleave`, and `drop`; it is keyboard-operable (role button, Enter/Space opens a visually hidden file input); a dropped real image previews as the "before" layer via `URL.createObjectURL` (revoke after use); a simulated ~1.4s "transform" runs `.ai-transform-animation` then announces completion — the entire flow is narrated in the live region.
- **Theme integrity:** red remains the dominant brand accent in both themes; gradients never reduce text legibility (scrim on the CTA band, accessible gradient stops on interactive surfaces).
